title: stream stitcher rewrite with anchored-boundaries and partial-json rescue
author: Imani Okafor
release_notes: Improve SSE reassembly: anchored boundary markers to avoid delimiter drift, partial-JSON rescue for truncated frames, and ordering guarantees for tool/function-call events. Backwards-compatible; opt-in strict mode behind flag 'stream.stitcher.strict'.
description:
Motivation: We continue to see production incidents where streaming ingestion produces truncated JSON objects or mis-ordered function-call sentinel emissions when event fragments split across network frames and backpressure windows. These manifest as partial JSON payloads that downstream consumers treat as terminal, or as tool calls arriving before the final assistant delta, causing client-side parse failures. This PR rewrites the stream stitcher to anchor frame boundaries and adds a deterministic partial-JSON rescue path.

What changed (high level):
- New stitcher core: replaces the incremental buffer heuristic with an anchored-boundary protocol that maintains a small ledger of boundary anchors (sequence anchor tokens emitted by the runtime) and uses them to align fragments before attempting JSON reconstruction. Anchors are lightweight and flow with existing SSE comments to avoid protocol changes.
- Partial-JSON rescue: when a JSON object cannot be parsed after coalescing, we attempt a conservative rescue that trims trailing incomplete UTF-8 sequences and applies token-aware re-synchronization heuristics to preserve at least one valid JSON subtree (useful for structured outputs and tool call payloads).
- Function/tool-call ordering: we added an ordering gate that delays emitting function-call sentinel events until the stitcher confirms the surrounding JSON span is well-formed or after rescue succeeds. This reduces false-positive tool invocations for split frames.
- Delimiter normalization: normalize mixed delimiter sequences (0x0A, 0x0D0A variants) emitted by different clients and proxies so chunk boundaries are not treated as message boundaries by mistake.
- Strict mode flag: introduced feature flag stream.stitcher.strict (default: false for compatibility). When enabled the stitcher fails fast on ambiguous anchors and surfaces a metrics tag to drive rollouts.

Why this approach: Previous fixes focused on ad-hoc coalescing and UTF-8 repair in multiple places which evolved divergent heuristics across language bindings. Consolidating logic into a single stitcher reduces duplication, centralizes metrics and observability, and provides a single opt-in path to tighten semantics without breaking existing clients. Anchors provide a minimal, backward-compatible signal that improves alignment accuracy under packet-loss and proxy chunking scenarios.

Commits (summary):
- Rewrite: introduce StreamStitcher with anchor ledger and resync algorithms (core rewrite).
- Parser: add partial_json_rescue utility and UTF-8 tail trimmer.
- OpenAI compat: gate function-call emission behind stitcher confirmation.
- Tests: add deterministic fuzz vectors and integration tests that simulate TCP-level splits and HTTP/2 push chunking.
- Docs: document stream.stitcher.strict and troubleshooting guide.

Files changed (high level):
- src/streaming/stream_stitcher.rs (new core implementation)
- src/openai_compat/sse_parser.py (normalize delimiters, call gating)
- tests/test_sse_framing.py (unit + fuzz harness)
- docs/compatibility/streaming.md (operational notes and flag docs)
- examples/compatibility/streaming_playground.rs (manual repros)
- tools/compat/test_vectors.json (new test vectors for fragmented frames)
- ci/flake_fuzz.sh (harness integration)

Testing and validation:
- Unit tests cover UTF-8 tail trimming, anchor ledger edge cases, and ordering gate scenarios.
- Integration tests run a local HTTP/2 chunker against both the legacy and new stitcher; observed a 96% reduction in partial-JSON error rates on the supplied corpus.
- Fuzz harness produced no regressions after 3 CI reruns; CI passed on Linux x86_64 and macOS runners.
- Canary rollout in internal staging for 24h with stream.stitcher.strict disabled; Prometheus metrics show decreased sse_parse_error_count and fewer tool-call-duplicates.

Observability and signals:
- New metrics: stitcher.anchor_misses, stitcher.rescue_attempts, stitcher.rescue_success, stitcher.emit_delay_ms.
- Logs: increased visibility when rescue path runs (log level DEBUG by default) and an INFO event when strict mode blocks emission.

Backward compatibility and rollout plan:
- Default behavior is backward-compatible: anchors are optional and stitched only when present; if anchors are missing we fall back to previous coalescing heuristics.
- Feature flag stream.stitcher.strict must be enabled per deployment to activate hard failure behavior. We will roll strict to canaries, then a small percentage cohort, and observe tool-call duplication and consumer parse errors.

Risks and mitigation:
- Risk: strict mode could surface parse failures for clients that rely on prior lenient behavior. Mitigation: strict is off by default and includes a clear metric tag to track breakage.
- Risk: performance regressions from extra ledger bookkeeping. Mitigation: microbenchmarks show <1.6% CPU overhead at p95 QPS with anchors enabled; we will monitor in Dedicated pods.

Checklist: 
- [x] Design doc reviewed (ENG-4829)
- [x] Unit + integration tests added
- [x] Fuzzing applied and CI green
- [x] Docs updated
- [x] Metrics instrumented

Notes for reviewers: focus on the anchor lifetime semantics in stream_stitcher.rs and on the gating logic in sse_parser.py. In particular, check that the ledger never grows unbounded (we evict anchors older than 2x median RTT) and that the rescue heuristic only returns JSON subtrees when they can be safely parsed without inventing keys.

Merge notes: Squash-merged after approvals. Canary rollout initiated immediately after merge with stream.stitcher.strict=false by default.
